question: A manufacturer sells an item to a wholesaler and makes a profit of 10%. The wholesaler sells the same item to a retailer at a profit of 12% .The retailer sells the same item to a customer at a profit of 15%. If the customer paid ₹21,252 for the item, then what was the cost price (in ₹) of the item for the manufacturer?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

By successive method

CP for manufacturer = 21252 × (100)/(115) × (100)/(112) × (100)/(110) = ₹15,000

∴ The cost price of the item for the manufacturer was ₹15,000.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

A manufacturer sells an item to a wholesaler at a profit of 10%

The wholesaler sells the same item to a retailer at a profit of 12%

The retailer sells the same item to a customer at a profit of 15%

The customer paid ₹21,252 for the item

Concept used:

SP = CP × (100+Profit)/(100)

Calculation:

CP to the retailer = 21252 × (100)/(115) = ₹18,480

CP to the wholesaler = 18480 × (100)/(112) = ₹16,500

CP to the manufacturer = 16500 × (100)/(110) = ₹15,000

∴ The cost price of the item for the manufacturer was ₹15,000.
